title: How Easy is Grade 7 Unseen Poetry
author: Dominic Salles
summary: Dominic Salles continues his series of graded unseen-poetry answers by taking the poem "Table" and the question of how the poet presents feelings about home and family. He restates his OTTER method (Opening, Technique, Technique, Ending, Review) as shorthand for writing an answer that is better than grade 5. He then shows a grade 5 response worth 12 marks, with examiner comments, and a grade 7 response worth 16 marks, with the methods highlighted in colour. For each, he supplies a checklist of the moves that separate the marks bands, such as quoting from the middle and ending of the poem, explaining the effect of key words and commenting on structure. The yellow and green highlights show what each answer is missing and why it stops where it does. The piece is a practical model-answer resource for teachers who want to make mark-scheme criteria explicit to students.
points: The OTTER structure gives students a short, memorable frame for an unseen poetry response, covering an opening link to purpose, two technique paragraphs, an ending and a structural review.
Pairing a grade 5 and a grade 7 answer on the same poem makes the difference between mark bands visible rather than abstract.
The checklists are distilled from reading dozens of scored answers, so teachers can use them directly as marking criteria and student self-assessment tools.
Highlighting what each answer omits shows students that higher marks come from doing more of the listed moves, not from writing differently.
quotes: This is my shorthand for how to write an answer. If you follow it, you will definitely write an essay which is better than grade 5!
This checklist spells out exactly what to do. It comes from reading dozens of answers at that scored 12 to 15 marks.
To push into the next grade band, the response needs to expand and elaborate on its ideas, specifically by diving deeper into the conflicting emotional layers experienced by the speaker
The table represents how family members held grudges, but also how their shared dinners at the table made them put aside their disagreements.
The response kicks off with references highlighting the speaker’s sense of discomfort, quickly elevating into a sustained Level 4 standard and staying there.
As you can see, if the student had followed all of OTTER, they would have scored much higher marks.
